title: CSuite Targets US and EU with Session Theft and RMM Abuse, Expanding Fraud and Access Risk
content_md: CSuite is emerging as a multi-stage phishing operation that combines Microsoft 365 session theft with remote access through legitimate management tools. ANY.RUN researchers linked 351 sandbox analyses to the campaign, with 51% of submissions coming from the United States. The activity has affected technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting organizations, while the mix of account compromise and endpoint access creates a clear path to mailbox abuse, fraud, and longer-term persistence inside business environments. How the CSuite Attack Chain Unfolds ANY.RUN sandbox sessions show a consistent pattern: the attack starts with a trusted business theme, passes through filtering and routing, and then moves toward either endpoint access or identity compromise. CSuite attack chain exposed by ANY.RUN experts 1. Lure delivery Victims receive Adobe Document Cloud shares or other business-themed messages impersonating services such as DocuSign, Zoom, Google Meet, Dropbox, and Microsoft 365. 2. Traffic filtering and routing Before the victim reaches the final page, redirectors can apply anti-bot checks and route users based on the email provider they enter. Microsoft, Google, and other accounts may be sent into different capture flows. 3. Counterfeit document page The victim lands on a fake document viewer designed to look like a legitimate business workflow. In sandbox sessions, these pages imitated Adobe Reader and DocuSign while keeping the actual document blurred or permanentl
